title: Parsing and Validation
definition: Parsing converts an external representation into structured data, while validation checks that the result satisfies required constraints.
purpose: Separate representation interpretation from syntactic and semantic acceptance decisions.
history: Parsers turn serialized representations into program values; validation layers then enforce structural and domain contracts before use.
mental_model: Parsing answers what the symbols represent; validation answers whether that represented value is acceptable here.
analogy: Reading a date from a form is different from deciding whether that date is allowed; the analogy fails when parsing itself can reject malformed syntax.
industry_notes: Validate all untrusted sources as early as practical, using explicit type, range, length, format, and business constraints.
ai_notes: AI often merges conversion with validation or overlooks empty input, NaN, infinities, Unicode, and cross-field constraints.
interview_notes: Ask for a case that parses successfully but fails semantic validation.
exercise_candidates: Classify parse failures and validation failures
